text:
Sophie: FYI — Acme told us their competitor just launched a 'fast-embed' offering and it's a gating factor for the pilot. They want lower embed latency. Quick sync: do we aim for a parity shim to win the pilot or double down on our long-term differentiator path? Need a decision by EOD.

Devon: Do we have the competitor's SLA/traffic shape? If it's pilot-scale tenant traffic we can probably ship a light shim (prefix caching + quantized embed model) as a short-term win.

Alex: Ran a couple of quick experiments yesterday. Quantized 8-bit embedder reduces cost ~30% but 99p latency goes up ~40ms compared to float. Batch sizing changes that a lot — with batch=8 it's pretty okay.

Priya: From Acme: they'd sign pilot if we match their competitor's 2x embed throughput. It's effectively gating sales.

Marcus: Framing options: (A) parity quickwin — ship shim + docs + scoreboard (fast but risky for focus), or (B) invest in a productized "low-latency embeddings tier" with controls and guarantees (slower to market but durable).

Sophie: Proposal: intermediate path — ship a limited canary shim for the pilot to hit parity, while we design the product tier in parallel. Suggested launch criteria for the shim: p95 embed latency < 120ms on pilot traffic, migration docs, telemetry hooks.

Devon: Eng estimate: ~2 sprints to get shim production-ready (autoscaling tweaks, KV prefix caching, kernel selection flags). Note: for stable p95 we probably need Dedicated GPU capacity for the pilot, otherwise noisy neighbors will blow the numbers.

Alex: Prototype command I used locally: `./run_embed --model rwd-embed-small-q8 --batch 8 --kv-cache true`. Observed p95 ~110ms on an A100-40G. Add `--continuous-batching` to squeeze more throughput. Multi-tenant tests push p95 to ~130ms.

Priya: :thumbsup: I'll tell Acme we can commit to a pilot canary with those targets. Need them to share expected concurrency/queries-per-min so we can size Dedicated.

Marcus: Flagging risk: shipping a shim creates support overhead and technical debt. Suggest we cap scope: pilot-only rollout and an automatic expiry in 90 days unless we productize it. Also define success metrics (conversion, latency delta, cost delta).

Sophie: Agreed. Action items: Devon + Alex -> draft shim spec + infra reqs (include Dedicated GPU request and fallback policy). Priya -> capture written gating conditions from Acme. Marcus -> draft scope-expiry clause + success metrics. I'll schedule a 30m to finalize details.

pm-bot: Meeting scheduled: #product-sync today 16:00 UTC. Link: https://cal.example/meet/abc123

Devon: I'll attach a rough perf plan and a spike checklist to this thread shortly.

Alex: Will upload a reproducible notebook and the raw p95 numbers (110ms local, 130ms multi-tenant). Also a short snippet showing kernel toggles we used.

Priya: Also note — legal will want to review SLA language if we promise a faster tier. That could add contracting time. cc @Marcus

Sophie: Thanks. If no objections, I'll mark priority as "high" for next sprint block for the shim canary and we'll treat the product tier as a parallel project with lower immediacy.

Devon: No objections from infra side.

Marcus: Sounds reasonable. Document guardrails and sunset behavior and we can greenlight.

Alex: One more note — add tracing hooks so we can segment pilot traffic and measure real-world p95 & cost per request. We'll need that to decide on productization.

Sophie: Perfect. I'll update the roadmap board and ping again after the 16:00 sync.
